sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Thames Valley Police Admits Warrantless Searches of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's Homes
cards.content: Thames Valley Police has admitted that the search warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes in February were unlawful. The police seized items during the search which are still being held. A further hearing is set for 2027 to decide whether the police can use the seized items as evidence. Mountbatten-Windsor who denies wrongdoing was arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office. He is challenging the warrants used in his arrest.

cards.title: Two Latvian men arrested at RAF base in Cambridgeshire
cards.content: Two Latvian men 36 and 32 years old were arrested at an RAF base in Cambridgeshire after a fence was breached. An abandoned vehicle was found near the base leading to a search and the discovery of a small fence breach. The men were initially arrested for trespass and criminal damage and then further arrested under the National Security Act for allegedly entering the site for a purpose that could harm the UK. Counter-terrorism police are investigating but so far there's no link to a recent incident at another RAF base.

cards.title: Anne Carson Wins Nobel Prize in Literature at Age 76
cards.content: Canadian poet and essayist Anne Carson has won this year's Nobel Prize in Literature. She's 76 years old and has written many books that blend poetry fiction and scholarship. The Nobel Prize committee praised her work for being bold and creative and for mixing old and new ideas together in new ways. Carson was surprised but happy when she found out and said she's grateful for the honor.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: UK MP Jess Asato Sues xAI Over AI Chatbot's Sexualized Images
cards.content: A UK Member of Parliament Jess Asato has criticized a US tech firm xAI after it failed to show up at a New York City Council meeting to discuss regulating AI developers. Asato is suing xAI over sexualized images of her created by its AI chatbot tool Grok. She claims xAI misused her private information and breached data protection rules. The meeting held on October 5 was a rare committee meeting where all council members were present.

cards.title: Manus AI agent startup raises $500 million despite deal block
cards.content: Manus an AI agent startup has raised over $500 million in its first funding round since Meta abandoned its acquisition of the company. This shows that investors are still confident in Manus despite the deal being blocked by Chinese authorities. The funding round was led by Boyu Capital and IDG Capital with existing investors Tencent HSG and ZhenFund also contributing. This means that Manus can continue to work on its AI agents which are designed to help users with tasks and provide information.

cards.title: Amazon Unveils New Alexa Tablets with Improved Speed, Design
cards.content: Amazon has launched a new range of Alexa tablets priced between $230 and $550. The devices are more expensive than previous models but Amazon says they're worth it because of their improved speed performance and design. The new tablets run Google's Android operating system unlike previous models which used Amazon's own app store. The company is hoping to make more money from its devices business and is banking on the new tablets to be a hit.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Nigerian pediatrician heads international cancer control union
cards.content: Dr Zainab Shinkafi-Bagudu a Nigerian paediatrician has been elected as the president-elect of the Union for International Cancer Control. She's the first African to lead the organization. Bagudu's election comes as cancer cases and deaths are projected to rise sharply with the greatest increases expected in poorer countries. She wants to focus on cancer care in low-income countries where health systems are already under pressure and to bridge the gap between these countries and the research technology and treatments being developed elsewhere.

cards.title: Russian lab worker dies from pneumonia, hundreds isolated
cards.content: A worker at a Russian lab that studies plague has died and hundreds of others have been isolated. The World Health Organization is trying to figure out what happened and if it's a risk to the public. The lab worker 28-year-old Darya Shipilova died from pneumonia of unknown cause. The Russian government initially didn't report the incident but the WHO found out and is now asking for more information. The WHO says the risk to the public appears to be low but they're still trying to determine the cause of the worker's death.

cards.title: WHO Investigates Death of Russian Lab Worker from Rare Plague
cards.content: The World Health Organization is trying to figure out what happened when a worker at a Russian lab died from a rare form of plague. The lab worker a 28-year-old woman was hospitalized and then died. Several hundred people who had contact with her are in quarantine. The WHO is concerned because the plague can spread from person to person. The organization is trying to get more information from Russia but has not received a response. The WHO has seen reports of a broken test tube in the lab but it's not clear if that's related to the worker's death.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: India's Monsoon Ends 13% Below Average Amid Worsening Drought Conditions
cards.content: India's southwest monsoon ended 13% below average but the situation on the ground is worse than the numbers suggest. In some states prolonged dry spells depleted soil moisture and crop losses have prompted drought declarations. Despite a relatively small national rainfall deficit severe drought conditions have emerged across parts of several states. Maharashtra Karnataka Rajasthan Andhra Pradesh and Telangana are among the worst-affected areas. Farmers are struggling with failed crops income losses and mounting debt while some are forced to sell cattle at distress prices due to fodder shortages. The government has declared drought in three states and many more are assessing their situation.

cards.title: Heavy Rain Hits Northern India, Snowfall Expected in Higher Himalayan Peaks
cards.content: Heavy rain hit Uttarakhand Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir with strong winds. Higher Himalayan peaks might see snowfall. Other areas got warnings for heavy rain thunderstorms lightning and strong winds. Delhi-NCR had cooler mornings and nights but hot days with possible thunderstorms and showers. Punjab Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh might see thunderstorms lightning and strong winds.

cards.title: Maharashtra declares 74% of talukas drought-hit due to dry monsoon season
cards.content: Maharashtra a state in India has declared around 265 talukas or about 74% as drought-hit due to a very dry monsoon season. To manage water scarcity the government has ordered a 10% water cut starting October 16. The state is also focusing on reusing treated wastewater for non-potable purposes like irrigation and industry. Currently only 57% of the state's sewage is treated and 17% of wastewater is reused which contributes to pollution in rivers and lakes.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: BBC Cuts Shows to Save £500m and Shift Focus to Digital
cards.content: The BBC is making changes to its Radio 4 programming to save £500m. The corporation will be cutting a number of shows including You and Yours Thinking Allowed and Free Thinking as well as reducing commissioning on its schedule and podcasts. However the BBC is also investing in new consumer and ideas programmes. The changes aim to focus investment on the BBC's digital platforms and reach more people beyond its own channels.

cards.title: Play Explores Challenges Faced by Men in Retirement, Tackles Mental Health
cards.content: A new play called The Corner Man explores the challenges men face when they retire from their sport or job using the story of a former boxer as an example. The play's writer and producer Cathal J Ferris was inspired by his own experiences with boxing and conversations with former fighters. The story looks at how men can lose their sense of purpose and struggle to talk about their mental health. Ferris wants the play to show that it's okay for men to open up and seek support from each other as it's an important part of dealing with life's changes.

cards.title: Gaten Matarazzo stars in London's West End production of Rent.
cards.content: Gaten Matarazzo known for his role as Dustin Henderson in Stranger Things has started a new job on London's West End playing Mark in the rock musical Rent. He says that not having to worry about getting every take right on stage is a relief unlike filming TV shows where you can have up to 30 takes. Matarazzo has a lot of experience in stage shows having performed on Broadway as a child and enjoys the structured schedule that comes with it. He's currently playing Mark a struggling filmmaker in Rent which explores the lives of young artists and friends living in 1980s and 1990s New York during the HIV/AIDS crisis.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Alberta to Hold Referendum on Independence or Staying in Canada
cards.content: Alberta a western Canadian province is set to hold a referendum on October 19th giving residents two options stay in Canada or move ahead with a formal binding referendum on independence at a later date. The vote's outcome could be crucial with some arguing that Alberta's economy would thrive independently while others predict significant costs and uncertainty.

cards.title: Tui Apologises for River Cruise Changes Due to Low Danube Water Levels
cards.content: Passengers who paid thousands of pounds for European river cruises with Tui were left angry after their itineraries changed involving hours spent on coach trips instead. Tui apologised blaming low water levels on the Danube and offered no refund. Passengers including Richard Pearson Sue Crosby and David Mallon described their disappointment feeling they were not getting the river cruise experience they booked. They spent a significant amount of time on coach trips and the scenery was missed.

cards.title: Chrysler Building gets $235 million makeover with art deco restoration
cards.content: The Chrysler Building a famous high-rise in Manhattan is getting a major makeover. The building's owner Cooper Union is selling the lease to developer Tishman Speyer which will spend $235 million to restore the building's art deco crown and facade. The renovation will also upgrade the building's mechanical systems and add a new lounge on the 61st floor.
